cases.name: Drake
cases.title: The Drake Curse
cases.tagline: The most famous fade in sports betting.
cases.summary: The biggest artist in the world is also the most public bettor alive — eight-figure stakes, posted slips, and a curse so consistent it has its own website. Teams he backs crumble. Fighters he walks out lose. The internet keeps the receipts.

timeline.text: Walks Conor McGregor to the cage at UFC 229. McGregor loses to Khabib. The curse is named.
Reported $1M on Argentina to win the World Cup final in regulation. Argentina wins the Cup — on penalties. Bet loses anyway.
Reported seven-figure stake on Israel Adesanya at UFC 281. Pereira stops Izzy in the fifth.
Reported $400K on Jake Paul against Tommy Fury. Fury by decision.
Reported ~$700K on the Chiefs in Super Bowl LVII. Kansas City covers. The curse takes a week off.
Reported $450K on Adesanya against Du Plessis at UFC 305. Submitted in the fourth.
Reported $355K on Mike Tyson against Jake Paul. Paul wins by decision.

cases.name: Dave Portnoy
cases.title: El Presidente
cases.tagline: A 30% hit rate that's somehow up $2.7 million.
cases.summary: Dave Portnoy bets the way he runs Barstool — loudly, publicly, and in seven figures. Across 30 publicly reported wagers the record is 9–21. The P&L is +$2.7M anyway, carried by three all-time futures cashes. Both facts are why America watches every slip he posts.

timeline.text: $500K on Virginia Tech +220 against Miami. Hokies lose. −$500K.
$1M on Michigan in the Rose Bowl CFP semi. Wolverines win it. +$847K.
$600K on UConn to win the NCAA Tournament at +360, DraftKings-confirmed. The Huskies run it back. +$2.16M.
$300K on Scottie Scheffler to win the Masters at +450. Green jacket. +$1.35M.
$1M on the Bills to win Super Bowl LIX. Buffalo falls short. −$1M.
$25K on a Caitlin Clark triple-double at +1300. She does it. +$325K.
$300K on the Ravens in the season opener. −$300K.
$1,000 side bet with Urban Meyer on Michigan. Even that one loses.

cases.name: Mattress Mack
cases.title: The Houston Hedge
cases.summary: Jim “Mattress Mack” McIngvale bets like nobody else on earth: nine-figure furniture promotions hedged with the biggest sportsbook wagers ever written. The tracked record is 3–17 across $86M in reported stakes — and he's up $23.5M anyway, headlined by the $72.6M Astros cash, the largest payout in U.S. legal betting history. When Mack bets, the whole city sweats with him.

timeline.text: $13M across books on the Astros to win the World Series. Nationals in seven. −$13M — his largest loss.
$3.46M on the Bucs +3.5 in Super Bowl LV at DraftKings. Tampa rolls. +$2.72M.
$9.5M on the Bengals moneyline in Super Bowl LVI. Rams by three. −$9.5M.
$8.8M on Kansas to win the NCAA title. Jayhawks cut down the nets. +$12.2M.
$10M across five books on the Astros to win the World Series. Houston does it — +$72.6M, the largest payout in U.S. legal betting history.
$8M in futures on the Astros to run it back. Rangers end it in the ALCS. −$8M.
$3.3M on the Patriots in Super Bowl LX, including the largest reported single at Caesars. Seattle spoils it. −$3.3M.
